proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 5.8 (p. 218): “a direct consequence of the Rectifiability 5.5, the Semi-continuity 3.7, and the Compactness Theorem 4.16 of Ch. 1 for Radon measures, and its proof is left to the reader”; the proof below is exactly that combination. ERRATUM (E1): 5.8's “liminf_{j→∞}” is taken along the extracted subsequence (the contract's form; along the full sequence the inequality can fail). The Compactness Theorem 4.16 of Ch. 1 is used in its corrected (second-countable, sequential) form, supplied by the sibling radon_compactness. Notation: μ_j = μ_{V_j} = (Vj j).weight, ‖δV_j‖ = variationMeasure (Vj j), G = Grassmannian N n, W ⊂⊂ U = IsRelCompactOpenIn W U (W open with compact closure in U).

Hypotheses: each V_j rectifiable (not needed below) with locally bounded first variation, sup_j(μ_j(W) + ‖δV_j‖(W)) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U, Θ^n(μ_j, x) exists and is ≥ 1 for x ∈ U ∖ A_j, and μ_j(A_j ∩ W) → 0 for every W ⊂⊂ U.
A1. Local mass bounds. Let K ⊆ U be compact (if K = ∅ there is nothing to prove). Let r := dist(K, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 0 (r := 1 if U = ℝ^N) and W := {y : dist(y,K) < r/2}; W is open and its closure lies in the compact set {y : dist(y,K) ≤ r/2} ⊆ U, so IsRelCompactOpenIn W U, and V_j.measure(K × G) = μ_j(K) ≤ μ_j(W) ≤ C_K := sup_j(μ_j(W) + ‖δV_j‖(W)) < ∞ for every j; this is the (uniform, hence eventual) local mass bound required by radon_compactness.
A2. Extraction (Ch. 1 4.16). The sibling radon_compactness applied to μ_j := V_j.measure (U is open: (Vj 0).isOpen_domain; A1 supplies its local mass hypothesis) gives a strictly increasing φ and V : Varifold N n U with ∫ f dV_{φ(j)} → ∫ f dV for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ U × G.
A3. Radon convergence on Gₙ(U). Every f ∈ C_c(U ×ˢ univ, ℝ) extends by zero to f̃ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f̃ ⊆ U × G (its support is a compact subset of the open set U × G), and ∫ f d(V_j).domainMeasure = ∫ f̃ dV_j.measure (V_j.measure = domainMeasure.map Subtype.val, Varifold.map_domainMeasure). Hence Varifold.RadonConverges (fun j ↦ V_{φ(j)}) V.
A4. Semicontinuity (3.7). Apply the sibling density_semicontinuity to the sequence V_{φ(i)}, the limit V and the sets B_i := A_{φ(i)}: RadonConverges (A3); each V_{φ(i)} has LBFV; liminf_i ‖δV_{φ(i)}‖(W) ≤ sup_j ‖δV_j‖(W) < ∞; Θ^n(μ_{φ(i)}, y) ≥ 1 on U ∖ B_i; μ_{φ(i)}(B_i ∩ W) → 0 (subsequence of a null sequence; W ⊂⊂ U ranges over open sets with compact closure in U). Conclusions: V has LBFV, ‖δV‖(W) ≤ liminf_i ‖δV_{φ(i)}‖(W) for every open W ⊂⊂ U (E1), and Θ^n(μ_V, x) exists and is ≥ 1 for μ_V-a.e. x.
A5. Rectifiability (5.5). Since Θ^n(μ_V,·) ≥ 1 > 0 μ_V-a.e., the sibling allard_tangent_cones (first conjunct, AllardRectifiabilityTheorem) gives IsRectifiable V. This proves CompactnessTheorem.
key_steps: Local mass bounds on compact subsets of U from the sup hypothesis; radon_compactness extracts a subsequence and a limit varifold V.
Extension by zero of test functions on Gₙ(U) gives RadonConverges (V_{φ(j)}) V.
density_semicontinuity (3.7) along the subsequence: V has LBFV, ‖δV‖(W) ≤ liminf_{j'} ‖δV_{j'}‖(W) (erratum: liminf along the subsequence) and Θ^n(μ_V,·) ≥ 1 a.e.
Allard's theorem 5.5 (allard_tangent_cones, first conjunct) gives IsRectifiable V.
